at_sea:
NOTHING IN FLIGHT. Voyage 6ec9b384b451 (the pickup phase says WHY a ticket is not moving) is PROVED at both seam ends and pushed, per Akien's standing mandate to progress it all the way through PROVED so his picture — and therefore his direction — is clearer.

WHAT SHIPPED. The phase slot's axis moved from WHO HOLDS IT to WHY IT IS NOT MOVING. _PHASES in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py grew from (waiting, in-process) to five: waiting, in-process, queued, hold, blocked. in-process is DERIVED, never stored (a git-tracked :in-process claims a hand that is gone once the session ends; Akien: 'stateless read on in-process makes sense to me'). Every WRITTEN phase carries a release FIELD, not prose, valid to deterministic detection — Akien: 'nothing passes a gate with prose. an inspector will not allow it.' The operator inbox sorts on the phase: hold and blocked IN (hold for awareness, blocked as escalation — his correction, overruling my read that hold was reference-not-inbox), waiting and queued OUT.

Both ends — cairn/tools/base and cairn/tools/operator_inbox — render: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-vocabulary-is-written-not-just-legal) -> [PROVED]. THE TERMINAL CARRIES NO PHASE: the 2026-08-07 ruling's core survives the widening word for word. Its multi-actor premise narrows because the fleet is one; Akien confirmed superseded-by-reframe, not violated ('exactly so').

Verdict 8/8 criteria, 9/9 hypotheses dispositioned. Build inspector: 34 findings, 0 red at both components. Both repos pushed and clean, verified by cairn.tools.orient.orient git.
next_direction:

Nothing to build; the probe reports.

2. THE FIRST USER IS CAST AND WAITING. That is the vocabulary's first real write and therefore the cheapest thing that moves the write rate off 0.0189.

3. NEEDS ITS OWN /intent, EXPLICITLY OUT OF THIS VOYAGE'S BOUNDS: the build inspector's second firing point at sail step 2.5. Akien's original intent was inspection right after the build — code smells, fields not filled in — so a miss costs an edit while still in the code rather than a round trip back from PROVEME. My post-PROVEME argument was about where the inspector LEARNS, which does not argue against a cheaper set firing earlier. Two firing points, one machine, different sieve sets, both hard, neither advisory.
